items.title: TokenEconomizer Cuts Coding-Agent Costs up to 31% by Learning Your Repo
items.summary: On November 17, UC Berkeley, Microsoft Research and Microsoft Security open-sourced TokenEconomizer, a plugin that lowers AI coding-agent costs by learning from past sessions in the same repository — without changing the agent or the underlying model. Profiling Claude Code on 60 SWE-Bench tasks showed waste clustered in three places: after five completed tasks in a repo, 30% of tool calls repeated an earlier action; 16 of 23 tools served every turn were never called; and the 17% of tasks that failed consumed 32% of spend. The plugin compresses recurring repo knowledge into one-line 'micro-skills', prunes unlikely-to-be-used tools, and detects failure loops to nudge the agent or alert the developer. Across 277 real SWE-Bench tasks spanning six repos and five agent-model combinations, average cost fell 18.4-30.9%, all 30 pairs saved money, and success rates stayed broadly stable; cumulative costs dropped below default from the sixth task onward.
items.impact: Cost, not raw capability, is becoming a first-class axis of coding-agent competition. Because the savings come from accumulated repo history and stay entirely on the developer's machine, this favors teams with stable codebases and rewards long-lived agent workflows over one-off tasks — and it needs no API key of its own.

items.title: xAI's Grok Build Puts Eight Parallel Subagents in One Session
items.summary: xAI has released an early test version of Grok Build, its first product aimed squarely at the agentic coding market, currently limited to the $300/month SuperGrok Heavy tier. A single session can spin up as many as eight parallel subagents working across different modules, branches or technical approaches. Its 'Arena Mode' then tournament-ranks the competing outputs against developer-specified criteria, turning a manual review of eight code drafts into a shortlist review while leaving the final choice to the human. The base model is xAI's grok-code-fast-1, scoring 70.8% on SWE-Bench Verified with a 256K-token context — competitive but not leading, which explains the emphasis on orchestration over single-pass accuracy. Grok Build is also strictly local-first: source code, credentials and project data stay on the developer's machine, with fine-grained file permissions, script-execution limits and configurable network controls that support fully air-gapped environments.
items.impact: Two design bets matter here. Arena choices become implicit preference data that trains the model — a private benchmark sampled from real engineering decisions. And local-first removes the 'does my code go to the cloud?' objection for finance, government and proprietary-code teams. Open questions: whether ranking criteria will be disclosed, and what eight-way parallelism costs in practice.

items.title: DeepMind's AlphaProof Code Formally Verifies Signal Down to Machine Code
items.summary: Google DeepMind unveiled AlphaProof Code, an agentic framework that mathematically proved key security properties of libsignal, Signal's encryption library, in the compiled AArch64 machine code that actually runs on devices — not just the protocol design or modified source. Human experts defined and reviewed the formal specifications; teams of 40-80 agents on Gemini 4 Carbon then wrote roughly 6.5 million lines of machine-checked Lean proof in four weeks with five researchers, none of whom wrote proof code by hand. The proofs cover the post-quantum PQXDH handshake and Triple Ratchet, establishing forward secrecy, authentication and post-compromise security. Agents flagged about 1% of the code for extra human review. As a sanity check, the team reintroduced two previously fixed real bugs; in both cases the system produced machine-checked proofs that the buggy version was insecure. Specifications and proofs are being released on GitHub.
items.impact: Formal verification has historically cost expert teams years — the seL4 microkernel took 20 person-years. This suggests proof-level assurance could become a line item a security team can price against an audit. Scope is narrow (one-to-one chats in a research build, not the Signal apps), and DeepMind says the next frontier is specification, not proof.

items.title: GXO Commits up to 1,000 Apptronik Humanoids to Its Warehouses
items.summary: GXO Logistics — the world's third-largest contract warehouse operator by floor area, with 221 million square feet serving brands like Apple, Nike and Hasbro — says it could deploy as many as 1,000 Apptronik humanoid robots across its facilities over the next four years, contingent on the results of ongoing pilots with Apptronik and Agility Robotics. The first units will handle e-commerce order picking and packing. Labor accounts for roughly two-thirds of GXO's expenses, and the company is also rolling out a workforce-management system that quantifies per-worker productivity. CEO Patrick Kelleher framed the robots as a complement rather than a replacement: employees will move toward tasks needing greater manual dexterity and higher-level judgment. Separately, GXO is pivoting toward higher-margin data-center, aerospace and defense supply chains, where complexity commands better returns.
items.impact: This is one of the largest concrete fleet commitments announced so far, and it comes from an operator with a direct cost incentive rather than a robot vendor. The 'pilot-gated' structure is telling: the humanoid business case in warehouses still has to be proven on throughput and uptime before the order converts.

items.title: Agile Robots Raises $500M at $8.5B Valuation to Scale Physical AI
items.summary: Munich-based Agile Robots closed a $500 million Series F at an $8.5 billion valuation, led by SoftBank Group with NVIDIA, Hitachi Group and T.Capital participating, bringing total invested capital to $2 billion. Founded in 2018 as a DLR spin-off, the company builds humanoids, mobile robots, arms and dexterous hands plus the AI models behind them, and reports more than 20,000 industrial solutions installed worldwide. Rather than betting on a single flagship humanoid, it generates revenue from force-controlled arms and mobile platforms while its humanoid and hand work matures — with subsidiaries Franka Robotics and Krause Automation extending the stack. The money is earmarked for U.S. expansion and production capacity, including its Fürstenfeldbruck plant near Munich, which has stated capacity for up to 10,000 legged and wheeled humanoids a year. A parts-sequencing proof of concept with Audi is underway at Ingolstadt.
items.impact: The round is explicitly a factory budget, not a research budget — a signal that investors are rewarding throughput over demos. It also highlights a strategic split: Agile's bet is that adoption comes incrementally through proven arms and mobile bases, not one dramatic foundation-model-powered launch. Capacity is not the same as deliveries; execution through 2027 is the test.
